newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar flat after 1997/98 budget presented.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar flat after 1997/98 budget presented.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar remained flat from closing levels around C$1.3546 (US$0.7382) in the early minutes after Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin delivered his government's 1997/98 fiscal budget, dealers said.
* They said trading flows were active and they expected the currency to strengthen on the deficit-fighting budget.

Nicholson said Scotia expected the currency to trade in a slightly stronger range over the next 12 hours, edging towards C$1.3510 (US$0.7402), after hitting weakness around C$1.3590 (US$0.7358) during trading on Tuesday.
"We expect the Canadian dollar to appreciate overnight as a result of the positive budget," Nicholson said.

Finance Minister Martin predicted the 1997/98 budget deficit would be C$17 billion, or two percent of gross domestic product. Spending for the year beginning April 1 was targeted by Martin at C$105.8 billion, with C$137.8 billion in revenue.
Martin estimated the 1996/97 budget deficit would be C$19.0 billion, compared to a projected C$24.3 billion. He predicted a 1998/99 deficit of C$9.0 billion.
Other foreign exchange players said the budget confirmed many of their expectations and that most of those had already been priced in ahead of the government's release.

"They started to rally the currency a little bit ahead of the budget," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange at CIBC-Wood Gundy Inc. "We went in feeling it was going to be a good news budget and that is pretty much the case."
"A lot of the (positive expectations) were built into the current levels, that's the caveat I would add," Wateridge said.
He said the Canadian dollar tracked the U.S. dollar today as it strengthened and then eased against the German mark.

"I think it's interesting that the low point for the Canada and high for the U.S. dollar matched the high for the U.S. dollar against the mark. The U.S dollar is off a couple pfennigs now and the Canada has rallied a little bit."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2456 marks in post-trading hours after closing in North America at 1.2442 marks and rose to 91.55 yen from 91.45 yen.
